name: KahaDB
tagline: Apache ActiveMQ Classic's built-in journal-plus-B-tree message store; a persistence engine, not a general DB.
description: KahaDB is the file-based persistence layer embedded in Apache ActiveMQ Classic: it arrived with ActiveMQ 5.3 in 2009 and has been the default message store since 5.4 (2010). Messages are appended to rolling journal files and located through a B-tree index kept in a page file, with checkpoints, checksums and recovery tooling to survive crashes; mKahaDB spreads destinations across several instances. It replaced the older AMQ Message Store with fewer file descriptors and faster recovery, and it ships with every ActiveMQ Classic release (6.3.2 in September 2026). You do not query KahaDB as a database: it exists to make broker messages durable, so it belongs on this list only as the storage engine behind a widely deployed broker.

scale.notes: One store per broker; multiKahaDB partitions destinations across instances; HA via shared-storage master/slave.

strengths: Append-only journal gives fast durable message writes
Default and battle-tested store for ActiveMQ Classic
Configurable checksums, checkpoints and corrupt-journal recovery
Zero extra infrastructure: lives in the broker's data directory
weaknesses: Not a general-purpose database; no query interface
Large backlogs or slow consumers can bloat journals and index files
Single-broker scope; HA relies on shared storage or replication of the broker
useCases: Durable message persistence for ActiveMQ Classic brokers
Example of a journal plus B-tree index storage design
